basis: 14 conversations from chat, 1–30 July (no Claude Code or Cowork)
statement: You integrate AI continuously into your work.
example: For instance, you come back to the same conversation over several days and build on it, rather than starting fresh each time.
straight_talk: You get moving fast and you keep going until the answer holds up — that's clear across the conversations. But you almost never check anything afterwards. You correct phrasing, not substance, and in the cases where a figure or a claim was wrong, it went through uncaught. This isn't about using AI less; it's the one place your workflow is missing a step.

areas.label: What you hand over
areas.summary: You hand over the routine work and keep what needs judgement.
areas.info: Choosing what AI takes on, and what you hold on to yourself.

quotes.text: I'll do the structure myself, but you can write a first draft of the sections

areas.label: How you ask
areas.summary: You set format and constraints up front, and correct quickly when the answer misses.
areas.info: How clearly you explain goal, format and examples, so the answer lands first time.

quotes.text: Write it as a table with three columns, and keep each line under 15 words
That's too long — same content, half the length, and drop the intro

areas.label: How you judge the answer
areas.summary: When the answer looks clean and confident, you often take it at face value.
areas.info: Reading the answer critically and catching errors — especially when it looks convincing.

areas.label: Care and data
areas.summary: Nothing in the conversations shows how you handle sensitive information.
areas.info: Using AI responsibly — checking facts and looking after sensitive information.

moves.text: When an answer looks right, stop and check one thing you can verify — a number, a name, a date — before you use it. That's exactly where over-trust creeps in.
Once a week, ask for the opposite: "what argues against this?" You'll spot fast where the answer was thin.

open_questions: What do you actually put into AI — and has the team agreed what's allowed?
When you use a figure or a claim from AI in something that goes further: who checks it?
epigraph: What moves you forward isn't using AI more — it's using it more deliberately.
